// THE COUNTERWEIGHT, and it is not decoration. A gate that reddens on everything is
// as useless as one that reddens on nothing, and this fixture is the assertion that
// the analyser can follow every shape production actually uses and stay SILENT:
//
//   - a channel handed into a struct's field and read back off that field;
//   - a channel handed to a package-local helper as an argument;
//   - a channel received on inside an AddReceive closure, through a helper;
//   - `any` targets and a *[]byte target, the two the SDK's binary/plain payload
//     can actually be assigned to;
//   - and a channel whose name NO messageBus.deliverSignal producer uses, receiving
//     into a concrete struct, which is CORRECT and must never be flagged. That is
//     the whole reason the rule is keyed on the NAME.
//
// The shapes mirror pumpnextactivity.go's pumpChannels / pumpPauseRequested /
// pumpReceiveSignalBlocking and billing/closecycle.go's chargeback receive.
package goodnormalised

const (
	signalOperatorPauseRequested = "operatorPauseRequested"
	signalActivityLeaseRequested = "activityLeaseRequested"
	// NOT a bus-delivered name: nothing calls messageBus.deliverSignal with it.
	signalChargebackReceived = "chargebackReceived"
)

type leaseChannels struct{ pause, lease workflow.ReceiveChannel }

type activityLeaseRequest struct{ ActivityID string }

type gatewayReversalEvent struct{ EventID string }

func GoodEntry(ctx workflow.Context) {
	pauseCh := workflow.GetSignalChannel(ctx, signalOperatorPauseRequested)
	leaseCh := workflow.GetSignalChannel(ctx, signalActivityLeaseRequested)

	// A directly-signalled channel with no bus producer. A concrete struct target is
	// right here, and the gate must say nothing about it.
	chargebacks := workflow.GetSignalChannel(ctx, signalChargebackReceived)
	var ev gatewayReversalEvent
	chargebacks.ReceiveAsync(&ev)

	goodLoop(ctx, leaseChannels{pause: pauseCh, lease: leaseCh})
}

func goodLoop(ctx workflow.Context, chans leaseChannels) {
	if paused := goodPauseRequested(chans.pause); paused {
		return
	}
	sel := workflow.NewSelector(ctx)
	sel.AddReceive(chans.lease, func(c workflow.ReceiveChannel, _ bool) {
		var req activityLeaseRequest
		_ = goodReceiveBlocking(ctx, c, &req)
	})
	sel.Select(ctx)
}

func goodPauseRequested(ch workflow.ReceiveChannel) bool {
	var raw any
	return ch.ReceiveAsync(&raw)
}

func goodReceiveBlocking(ctx workflow.Context, ch workflow.ReceiveChannel, out *activityLeaseRequest) bool {
	var raw any
	ch.Receive(ctx, &raw)
	return goodDecode(raw, out)
}

func goodDecode(raw any, out *activityLeaseRequest) bool {
	m, ok := raw.(map[string]any)
	if !ok {
		return false
	}
	id, ok := m["ActivityID"].(string)
	out.ActivityID = id
	return ok
}

// GoodRawBytes takes the OTHER assignable target: the SDK's ByteSlicePayloadConverter
// can hand a binary/plain payload to a *[]byte, so this loses nothing.
func GoodRawBytes(ctx workflow.Context) []byte {
	ch := workflow.GetSignalChannel(ctx, signalOperatorPauseRequested)
	var b []byte
	ch.Receive(ctx, &b)
	return b
}
